g.text: §3 CAPABILITY COVERAGE · §4 APPLICATIONS
Three contexts span the dissemination spectrum on one pipeline: a
camera-ready week, a lab's intake, a course's weekly packs
Who runs it, which artifacts they lean on, what they revise; Tables 2–3 audit what the video and blog generators emit
§4.1 The author's last mile
ONE-OFF, SINGLE PAPER
One Claude Code session per paper: one extraction pass
populates the bundle, then the three generators emit an editable
.pptx, a synchronized video.pptx + .mp4 pair, and a bilingual
Word .docx pair the author hand-revises rather than
regenerates — all navigable through one reel.html that doubles
as a review surface for co-authors.
LEANS ON
editable .pptx poster
video.pptx + .mp4 pair
bilingual .docx pair
reel.html as a review surface
§4.2 Lab and org communication
CONTINUOUS, PER ACCEPTED PAPER
Wired into the publication-intake pipeline so every accepted
paper auto-generates draft dissemination artifacts an editorial or
communications team then polishes. The editable PowerPoint
and Word outputs make it a draft-and-revise workflow; the
bilingual blog covers a Chinese-WeChat and an English
research-blog register from one evidence map.
LEANS ON
draft artifacts per accepted paper
PowerPoint and Word for hand-off
one reel per paper for the comms team
§4.3 Educational reuse
PERIODIC, MANY-PAPER BATCH
A course, reading group, or public-understanding outlet feeds a
reading list through the pipeline to produce paper-of-the-week
briefing packs: a lecture deck, an asynchronous talk video, a
newsletter blog. Instructors adjust framing or drop a slide;
re-running on a corrected PDF re-issues the whole pack.
LEANS ON
lecture deck
asynchronous talk video
newsletter blog
versioned bundle per paper
CAPABILITY AUDITS, TABLES 2 AND 3
Table 2 (video) asks whether a system emits visual attention cues or cursor grounding, an editable
PPTX deck, duration control, and narration audio; Table 3 (blog) asks about layout checks, embedded
figures, editable DOCX output, and paper-input summarization.
The audited products and research systems generally cover a single artifact; ResearchStudio-Reel
emits all three, exposes the shared bundle, includes a native-editable source in each package, and
stitches them into one surface. The audit documents breadth of the contract; it does not measure editing
effort or the viewer's usability.
GAP TO HUMAN POSTERS
Matching or exceeding the aggregate judge scores does not mean the output is on par with an author's own
poster. A human designer routinely adds material the paper does not contain — a purpose-drawn method or
overview diagram, explanatory icons — whereas the pipeline is grounded in the extracted bundle and reuses
only figures and content that appear in the paper. Author taste also spans a wide, legitimate range; the pipeline
analyses each paper's figure and content profile and chooses the layout that fits it, aiming for a sensible middle
ground rather than any single house style.
Source: arXiv:2607.04438 v2 (19 Jul 2026)
